annotations.text:
Round two. The first five were one layout in five palettes — three stacked panels, wall on top, hand at the bottom — so they were not really a choice.
These five change the LAYOUT first and the palette second. Same turn in all of them (The Fridge V3, sloper / the blank / smear edge, Open Hand / Lock Off / Smear, pump 7 of 11, preview WORKS IT · 2 grip left · +1 pump) so the structure is the only variable.

F · VERTICAL ASCENT — no panels at all: the screen IS the wall.
A full-bleed rock face with sky at the top, holds placed where they physically are, a climber silhouette mid-move between them, pump as a gauge down the left edge, hand fanned as three overlapping cards over the bottom.
Trade: the only one where height and progress are felt rather than read — and the hardest to keep legible, since every number sits on drawn rock.

G · RING — radial, built around the thumb.
Pump becomes the arc of a dial with the number in its centre; the three holds are spokes off it; the hand curves along the bottom edge where a thumb actually reaches, one card raised as the held one. Play is a drag from the arc to a spoke.
Trade: genuinely one-handed and unlike any card game on the store — but the ring costs a lot of screen for three holds, and a fourth lane would crowd it.

H · ARCADE — the route is an opponent, not a document.
VS header with two health bars (your pump vs the route's remaining holds), skewed neon plates, a round/flow banner, and the preview shouting as a hit confirm. Cards are a move list.
Trade: the most energy and the clearest stakes of the five; also the furthest from the sport — this is a fighting game wearing climbing, and Halloway's fiction has nowhere to live in it.

I · ZINE — photocopied black-and-white, everything hand-cut.
Ransom-note masthead, holds as clippings taped down the page at angles, pump as a row of hand-inked blocks, the verdict scrawled across the collage, hand taped along the bottom. Two inks, no gradients.
Trade: the strongest personality here and cheap to produce forever — the rotations and dashed rules cost some scanability, and it is a loud voice to commit a whole game to.

J · TERMINAL — the whole game as one text readout.
CRT green on black, scanlines, everything in one monospace column: route, gauges as ASCII bars, holds and hand as an indexed list, the preview as a labelled DRY RUN block showing its own arithmetic (6 - 4, 2 bite - 1 static), and a command line at the foot.
Trade: it explains its own maths better than anything we have shipped, and it is the only layout that would survive twelve holds. It is also a deliberate wall — no image of climbing at all.
